newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar seen stabilising after strong jobs data.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar seen stabilising after strong jobs data.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar is likely to stabilise around current levels after stronger than expected employment data put paid to its recent slide, analysts said on Tuesday.
Monetary conditions tightened on Tuesday after markets were caught off guard by data showing more of a rebound in June quarter jobs growth than most had forecast.
Statistics New Zealand said seasonally adjusted employment grew 0.2 percent in the June quarter, against economists' average forecast of a 0.15 percent fall.
A 2.5 percent quarterly rise in the number of hours worked also shocked economists, who had suggested the Reserve Bank of NZ's (RBNZ) forecast of a 1.9 percent rise was too high.
By early afternoon the kiwi dollar had risen to US$0.6440/47 from 0.6427/34 just before the data's 10.45 a.m. release, while short term interest rates rose four pips to 8.34 percent.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell chief economist Ulf Schoefisch told Reuters Financial Television the kiwi was showing "interesting resilience" around current levels.
